tasks.short: Report work, disturbances and unusual events to supervisors

steps.what: Gather observed work quality, quantity, disturbances, rule violations and unusual occurrences
Prepare and check written reports of inmate work and unusual occurrences
Provide supervisors oral and written reports and explain relevant context

tasks.design: Configure a clear report form in the {OTHER} institutional record system, with existing identifiers reused where checked. The officer captures and verifies all substantive facts, then submits the exact checked report and briefs the supervisor; no generated allegations or automated disciplinary action is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated headings and identifiers can add effort to otherwise substantive report writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reduce formatting without relying on model-written evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Separating observation, another person's account and interpretation of an event.
tasks.human_edge: The officer provides context, acknowledges uncertainty and answers the supervisor's questions.
tasks.altitude: A small formatting reduction; reporting judgement and briefing remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check whether an event report distinguishes observation from inference

evidence.claim: The digest reports a Draft One randomised trial in which reports were not written faster. It does not justify assuming that model drafting saves correctional reporting time.
Native form configuration may remove repeated formatting, but the small proposed saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is focal officer fact preparation, writing and supervisor briefing, not observation patrols, supervisory assessment or disciplinary decisions.
Officer s1 produces checked observations and counts directly, retaining all 35 hours. No structured violation or severity code is assumed to be available for free.

Officer s2 captures event date/time, location, verified person references, work quantity/units, observed quality, source attribution, factual narrative and uncertainty. Capture, factual checking and exception handling retain 28 hours.

Existing roster and shift records have their usual officer or records-team producers; no additional entry or new monitoring is imposed. Missing identifiers lead to manual verification, never an inferred match.
Test native forms and defaults before custom code. Only repeated formatting and identifier navigation can shrink; substantive writing and meaning checks remain human.
unknowns: Applicable institutional data and reporting rules
research_questions: Does native form configuration save time after complete factual capture and final report checks?

already_counted.description: Capture report facts, check meaning and correct entries
Final submission check and oral briefing

incremental.description: Maintain form definitions and checked defaults

approvals.approved_version: Exact report ID/version, facts, source attribution and intended supervisor recipient checked before submission; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+28+30=93. Gross 7 less 1 upkeep gives net 6. Low assumes native forms already remove formatting friction; high requires that friction within the 35-hour writing slice. Fact preparation and briefing keep all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel inmates and respond to concerns

steps.what: Counsel inmates and respond to legitimate questions, concerns and requests

tasks.design: Keep the officer's conversation and response personal. Approved procedures in the {DOCS} can support an answer as today; no chatbot assesses whether a concern is legitimate or replaces supportive contact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Concerns depend on trust, current circumstances and the officer's authority.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change is proposed for this contact boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising an urgent concern and escalating without dismissing the person.
tasks.human_edge: The officer listens and responds to the actual situation.
tasks.altitude: Contact time and response responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify the escalation route for an unresolved welfare concern

evidence.claim: Supportive contact and contextual response remain human work; this design claims no saving from substituting an automated answer.

assumptions: Boundary is counselling and responding, not separate case-note writing or request tracking. Work remains within officer competence.
The inmate produces questions and concerns directly. No structured legitimacy or welfare-risk flag is assumed.
Existing native reference access remains sufficient; no new recording or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Local response and welfare referral procedures
research_questions: Which unresolved requests need clearer human escalation routes?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100 with incremental=0. Routine questions and sensitive concerns retain direct contact time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign inmate duties and explain instructions

steps.what: Assign duties to inmates and provide instructions suited to the actual work

tasks.design: Retain duty allocation and instruction with the officer. Existing permitted restrictions in the {OTHER} institutional record system inform the decision; no matching score or automatic work allocation is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Allocation depends on current conditions, permitted restrictions and understandable instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change is required for this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing safe work, authorised restrictions and the need to explain the task clearly.
tasks.human_edge: The officer checks understanding and responds to practical concerns.
tasks.altitude: Assignment authority and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify responsibility for an unusual duty restriction

evidence.claim: Contextual duty allocation and instruction are retained human work, without an invented roster-administration baseline.

assumptions: Boundary is assignment and explanation, not separately performed roster preparation or work reporting.
Required work and authorised restrictions come through existing responsible staff; the officer checks current conditions directly. No new structured suitability score is assumed.
Existing native record access is unchanged; no extra data capture, software or upkeep is proposed, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Permitted duty allocation responsibilities and restrictions
research_questions: Where do duty instructions need clearer explanation or human escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and incremental=0. Assignment judgement and personal instruction retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Issue authorised clothing, tools and items

steps.what: Check authorisation and issue clothing, tools and other items to inmates

tasks.design: Keep item checks and physical issue with the officer. Existing issue permissions in the {OTHER} institutional record system can be consulted as today without creating a new automatic entitlement or handover process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual identity, authorisation and physical items must be checked at issue.
tasks.enabler_now: No software change is proposed to this hands-on boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Handling restricted items and recognising an inconsistent request.
tasks.human_edge: The officer checks the recipient and actual items before handover.
tasks.altitude: Issue responsibility and physical service time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve an unclear authorisation for an item request

evidence.claim: Physical issue and contextual authorisation checks remain human work; no extra record slice is assumed for savings.

assumptions: Boundary is checking and handing over authorised items, not a separately assigned inventory-report task.
Existing authorised staff provide issue permissions through normal procedures; officer checks recipient and items directly. No structured permission feed for automation is assumed.
Native reference access remains as today. No new capture, code or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Local item issue and authorisation procedures
research_questions: Which requests most often require a supervisor to clarify permission?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; incremental=0. Routine and restricted-item issues retain physical and checking time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain inmate contact, duty assignment and physical issue while reducing a small report-formatting slice where it exists.
reach: Review report source attribution and unresolved concerns with a correctional supervisor
role.ambitious_version: Provide traceable, carefully checked reports while preserving direct contact and accountable institutional decisions.
